title: Exercise 7A · Q9(a)
summary: Find TH in ΔTHV; the tick marks give UH = TH; then find TU in ΔTUH.
alt: Exercise 7A · Q9(a): In the figure, TH ⊥ UV, UH = TH, TV = 34 cm and HV = 30 cm. Find the value of a, the length of TU.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: In the figure, **TH ⊥ UV** and the tick marks show that **UH = TH**. **TV = 34 cm** and **HV = 30 cm**. We have to find **a**, the length of **TU**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔTHV, **∠H = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **TV**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides. We want a shorter side, so subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TV^2} &= \role{legA}{HV^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TV^2} - \role{legA}{HV^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and subtract
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and subtract.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TV^2} &= \role{legA}{HV^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TV^2} - \role{legA}{HV^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{34^2} - \role{legA}{30^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1156} - \role{legA}{900} \\ &= \role{legB}{256}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TV^2} &= \role{legA}{HV^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TV^2} - \role{legA}{HV^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{34^2} - \role{legA}{30^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{1156} - \role{legA}{900} \\ &= \role{legB}{256} \\ \role{legB}{TH} &= \sqrt{256} = 16\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Use the tick marks
steps.narration: The tick marks say **UH = TH**, so **UH = 16 cm** as well.\[\begin{aligned}UH = TH = 16\ \text{cm}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔTUH, **∠H = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **TU**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{TH^2} + \role{legB}{UH^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and add
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and add.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{TH^2} + \role{legB}{UH^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{16^2} + \role{legB}{16^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{256} + \role{legB}{256} \\ &= \role{hyp}{512}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 512 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{TH^2} + \role{legB}{UH^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{16^2} + \role{legB}{16^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{256} + \role{legB}{256} \\ &= \role{hyp}{512} \\ \role{hyp}{TU} &= \sqrt{512} = 16\sqrt{2} = \role{ans}{22.6\ \text{cm}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check TH
challenges.prompt: In ΔTHV, TV = 34 cm and HV = 30 cm. Find **TH**.

takeaways: Pythagoras' theorem works only in **right-angled** triangles — mark every right angle in the figure first.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
